newsitem.title: MEXICO: GM sees Mexico auto market up in 1997.
newsitem.headline: GM sees Mexico auto market up in 1997.

text.p: Mexico's auto market could grow to more than 400,000 in 1997 from about 330,000 in 1996, the president of the General Motors Mexico division said on Wednesday.

"We are saying that, if the current economic situation continues, that if there is downward pressure on interest rates, a stable peso and increased liquidity, I think the market will go over 400,000 units this year in total," Cowger told a news conference.
According to the Mexican Association of the Automobile Industry, 333,932 autos were sold wholesale in 1996.
That was up dramatically from 184,937 in 1995, a year of economic crisis in Mexico. But both the 1996 sales and the 1997 projection by GM fall short of the 598,087 wholesale sales in pre-crisis 1994.
GM controlled 29 percent of the Mexican market share in the first two months of the year, Cowger said.
General Motors de Mexico, 61 years old, makes cars for the domestic and export markets from three plants in Mexico.

"We will continue with the same exportation plans that we had last year," Cowger said. "As you know, we took an agressive stand on exporting and developing new markets in Central America, in the Caribbean, in South America. We are currently working on another program where we will expand to the Far East."
